title: Scalar squares for the twisted pullback comparison of a Cartesian square
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a_0\geq1$, and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p^{a_0}}$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure. Let $X,X',Y,Y'$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let $u:X'\to X$, $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $v:Y'\to Y$ form a Cartesian square $f\circ u=v\circ f'$ [def-pc-base-change], where $f$ is smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ and $v$ is arbitrary. Use $\mathcal C_R(W)=D^b_c(W,R)$, for $R=E,L$, in the raw rationalization convention [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], derived pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and exact scalar extension $T_W=T_{L/E,W}$ with its specified pullback comparisons $p_{h,M}:T_{\mathrm{source}(h)}Lh_E^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh_L^*T_{\mathrm{target}(h)}M$ from [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Put $D_W^R(M)=M(d)[2d]$ and $H_{h,R}=D_{\mathrm{source}(h)}^RLh_R^*$ for $h=f,f'$. Let $q_{W,M}:T_WD_W^EM\xrightarrow{\sim}D_W^LT_WM$ be the canonical tensor, twist and shift comparison, and put
$$a_{h,M}=D_{\mathrm{source}(h)}^L(p_{h,M})\circ q_{\mathrm{source}(h),Lh_E^*M}.$$

For a morphism $h$ let $c^R_{h,g}:L(g\circ h)_R^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh_R^*Lg_R^*$ be the canonical pullback composition comparison transported from the integral construction, as in [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange]. Put
$$U_R=Lu_R^*Lf_R^*,\quad V_R=Lf'_R{}^*Lv_R^*,\quad t_R=c^R_{f',v}\circ(c^R_{u,f})^{-1}:U_R\xrightarrow{\sim}V_R,$$
using $f\circ u=v\circ f'$. Let $z^R_{u,M}:Lu_R^*D_X^RM\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X'}^RLu_R^*M$ be the canonical pullback/tensor comparison followed by pullback of the twist line and the shift comparison from [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange]. Define
$$P_U=Lu_L^*(p_f)\circ p_{u,Lf_E^*(-)},\qquad P_V=Lf'_L{}^*(p_v)\circ p_{f',Lv_E^*(-)},$$
$$m_R=D_{X'}^R(t_R)\circ z^R_{u,Lf_R^*(-)}:Lu_R^*H_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{f',R}Lv_R^*,$$
$$r_A=Lu_L^*(a_f)\circ p_{u,H_{f,E}(-)},\qquad r_B=H_{f',L}(p_v)\circ a_{f',Lv_E^*(-)}.$$
Then, for every $M\in\mathcal C_E(X)$ and $K\in\mathcal C_E(Y)$, the actual specified comparisons satisfy
$$z^L_{u,T_XM}\circ Lu_L^*(q_{X,M})\circ p_{u,D_X^EM}=D_{X'}^L(p_{u,M})\circ q_{X',Lu_E^*M}\circ T_{X'}(z^E_{u,M}),\tag{Z}$$
$$P_V\circ T_{X'}(t_E)=t_L\circ P_U,\tag{C}$$
$$z^L_{u,Lf_L^*T_YK}\circ r_{A,K}=D_{X'}^L(P_{U,K})\circ q_{X',U_EK}\circ T_{X'}(z^E_{u,Lf_E^*K}),$$
$$r_{B,K}=D_{X'}^L(P_{V,K})\circ q_{X',V_EK},$$
$$r_{B,K}\circ T_{X'}(m_{E,K})=m_{L,T_YK}\circ r_{A,K}.\tag{M}$$
All are equalities of natural transformations. The twist-line maps in (Z) are the ones induced by pullback of roots-of-unity sections and extension of their coefficients; for $d=0$ they are the coefficient-unit maps. The comparison $a_h$ displayed above agrees, for smooth $h=f,f'$, with the rationalization of $a$ in [lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality].

These squares have the unit, tower and shift coherence of the specified scalar comparisons. Explicitly, for $E\subset F\subset L$ and any one of the comparison families $q,p,P_U,P_V,a,r_A,r_B$, write it as $w_{J/I}:T_{J/I,W}F_I\to F_JT_{J/I,V}$, where $F_R$ is respectively $D_W^R$, $Lh_R^*$, $U_R$, $V_R$, $H_{h,R}$, $Lu_R^*H_{f,R}$ or $H_{f',R}Lv_R^*$, with its indicated input scheme $V$ and output scheme $W$. These maps satisfy
$$w_{L/E,K}\circ\alpha^{\mathrm{in}}_K=\alpha^{\mathrm{out}}_K\circ w_{L/F,T_{F/E}K}\circ T_{L/F}(w_{F/E,K}),$$
where $\alpha^{\mathrm{in}}_K=\alpha^W_{L,F,E,F_EK}$ and $\alpha^{\mathrm{out}}_K=F_L(\alpha^V_{L,F,E,K})$, with $\alpha^W_{L,F,E}:T_{L/F,W}T_{F/E,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{L/E,W}$ the tensor associator. For $E=L$ these are the canonical unit maps. Under the canonical shift comparisons, $w_{K[1]}=w_K[1]$, and (Z), (C), (M) commute with all these identifications. The line defining the $d$-fold Tate twist has degree zero, so these equations introduce no extra cochain sign. No exceptional inverse image or exceptional base-change theorem occurs in (Z), (C), or (M).

proof.text: The finite-type schemes over the field are locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, hence Noetherian. Their topological Krull dimensions have finite natural bounds. The coefficient prime is a unit in every stalk by the structure map from B.k. Locally finite type descends along f followed by the structure map; quasi-compactness follows from the Noetherian source. Base change gives the separation, local finite type and relative dimension of f′. Build the Geometry record with these actual conclusions.

Use the normalized coefficient coherence theorem to obtain the common ShiftCoherence s, SquareCoordinates, TowerCoherence and SquareShiftEquations. Use the primitive scalar theorem at each finite inclusion to obtain Z, C and Naturality.

Expand rA and a; naturality of z at p_f moves D(p_f) across z. Substitute Z at f_E^*K and use D.map_comp to combine p_u and u_L^*(p_f) into PU. This is the first intermediate equation. Expand rB and a; D.map_comp gives the second intermediate equation with PV.

Expand m inside T and replace rB by q followed by D(PV). Naturality of q at t_E moves T(D(t_E)) across q. Combine the two D maps and substitute C to get D(PU followed by t_L). Split the D map and substitute the first intermediate equation backwards. Reassociation leaves rA followed by z_L and D(t_L), exactly rA followed by m_L. This proves M, while the primitive theorem supplies Naturality.

Ordinary scalar extension preserves the finite-Tor constructible domains at both vertices by scalar_preserves in AdicOperationSource. Its functor is completedDerivedScalarExtension; the framework/PBC bridge supplies its natural isomorphism with integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar. A proved private lemma transports bounded constructibility and the common Tor interval along that isomorphism. Thus ScalarClosed holds for the actual functors used in the conclusion. Apply the one-arrow adic identification with these closures and s.atX, s.atX′ for f and f′. Package all conclusions in the unchanged Conclusion.
